title: Best Dehumidifier with Drain Hose (2026): Gravity-Drain Picks
h1: The Best Dehumidifiers with a Drain Hose
dek: Got a floor drain? Then you don't need a pump. Thread on a garden hose, run it downhill and never empty a bucket again.
description: The best dehumidifier with a drain hose port for basements and single rooms, plus how to set up a gravity drain hose so it flows reliably all season.
intro: A dehumidifier drain hose is the simplest upgrade you can make to a basement or utility-room setup. If there's a floor drain, a sump pit or any opening lower than where the unit sits, you can thread an ordinary garden hose onto the drain port, run it downhill and let gravity do the work. No bucket to empty, no overflow shutoffs, and no pump motor to fail.

That last part matters. Pump models cost more and add a part that can clog or wear out. When the geometry allows it, a gravity drain does the same job for less. Every pick below drains through a standard garden-hose connection; the trick is choosing the right capacity for your space and setting up the hose so water keeps flowing.

We compared models using DOE 2019 ratings, manufacturer manuals and spec sheets for drain-port details, ENERGY STAR data and owner-review patterns. We don't lab-test; figures here are published ratings.
topPicksLead: The **Midea Cube 50** is our top gravity-drain pick: a standard garden-hose port, low published power draw and enough capacity for most basements.

blocks.text: That universal thread size means any basic garden hose fits, and you can swap hoses between brands. The only real requirement is that the hose runs downhill the whole way.

sections.heading: How we pick dehumidifiers with a drain hose

blocks.text: We confirmed each model's drain-port design and thread size in its manual, then compared DOE 2019 capacity, rated coverage, ENERGY STAR status and low-temperature operation. Since a hose-drained unit tends to run for long stretches, we gave extra weight to efficiency.
We also scanned owner reviews for drain-related complaints — leaking ports, hoses that slip off, internal screens that clog — and checked the CPSC recall database. We don't run our own tests.

sections.heading: What to look for in a dehumidifier with a drain hose connection

items.label: A drain lower than the unit
items.text: Gravity only works downhill. If the nearest drain or sink is higher than the port, buy a [pump model](/best/best-dehumidifier-with-pump/) instead.

items.label: A standard hose thread
items.text: A 3/4-inch garden-hose port lets you use any hose, cut to length.

items.label: A port that disables the bucket
items.text: On most units, connecting the hose bypasses the bucket. Check the manual for whether you must remove a plug or insert a fitting.

items.label: Right-sized capacity
items.text: Match pints to space and dampness with our [dehumidifier size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/).

items.label: Efficiency
items.text: Hose-drained units often run nonstop. ENERGY STAR certification and a low published wattage keep running costs down.

sections.heading: How to set up a dehumidifier drain hose

items: **Check the geometry.** The drain port must sit higher than the hose's end point. Raising the unit on a sturdy stand or block can create the slope you need.
**Connect the hose to the port.** Remove any cap or plug, attach the supplied adapter if your model uses one, and thread the hose on hand-tight.
**Keep a continuous downhill slope.** Any sag that dips below the port lets water pool and stall. Clip or zip-tie the hose along its route.
**Cut it to length.** Excess hose coiled on the floor traps water. Shorter is better.
**Aim the end into the drain,** not just near it, and secure it so it can't flip out.
**Inspect monthly.** The port has no motor, but the screen inside can collect dust. A quick rinse keeps flow steady.

blocks.title: Water still filling the bucket?
blocks.text: The hose probably has a dip or kink, or the port's internal fitting isn't seated. Straighten the run and check the manual's drain-setup diagram. If the unit stops collecting water entirely, see our [troubleshooting guide](/guides/dehumidifier-not-collecting-water/).

sections.heading: Drain hose tips for Midea, Frigidaire, GE and Hisense

blocks.text: Midea, Frigidaire and GE all specify a standard 3/4-inch garden-hose thread on their drain ports, so a regular hose fits. Some models ship with a short adapter or require you to remove a rubber plug behind the bucket first. Hisense and most other brands follow the same garden-hose approach, but always check your manual for the exact port location and any adapter.

items: **Hose too short?** A longer garden hose or a dedicated dehumidifier drain hose of any length works, as long as it slopes downhill.
**Leaking at the port?** Add a fresh hose washer; worn washers are the most common cause.
**Basement without a floor drain?** A sump pit or a condensate pump can be the destination. Our [where to place a dehumidifier](/guides/where-to-place-a-dehumidifier/) guide covers layout options.

blocks.text: The **Midea Cube 50** is the best dehumidifier with a drain hose for most homes: efficient, well sized for basements and fitted with a standard garden-hose port. Save money with the **hOmeLabs HME031003N** if a floor drain is in reach, pick the **Frigidaire FHDD5034W1** for a persistently wet basement, or size down to the **GE ADEL35LZ** or **Frigidaire FFAD2233W1** for smaller rooms. Just confirm your drain sits lower than the unit before you buy. For basement-specific advice, see our [best dehumidifier for basement](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-basement/) guide.

faqs.q: What is the best dehumidifier with a drain hose?
faqs.a: The Midea Cube 50 (MAD50S1QWT). Its rear port accepts a standard 3/4-inch garden hose, its published power draw is about 512 watts at 50% humidity, and it's rated for up to about 4,500 square feet.

faqs.q: What size hose fits a dehumidifier drain?
faqs.a: Most dehumidifiers, including every model here, use a standard 3/4-inch garden-hose thread. Any ordinary garden hose or a dedicated dehumidifier drain hose will fit.

faqs.q: What's the best basement dehumidifier with a drain hose?
faqs.a: For most basements, a 50-pint unit like the Midea Cube 50 or Frigidaire FHDD5034W1 connected to a floor drain or sump. If the basement is very large, the hOmeLabs HME031003N claims the widest coverage.

faqs.q: What's the difference between a drain hose and a pump?
faqs.a: A drain hose uses gravity, so the port must be higher than the drain and the hose must slope downward. A pump uses a small motor to push water up to a sink or window. Gravity drainage is cheaper and has nothing to wear out.

faqs.q: Why is my dehumidifier drain hose not draining?
faqs.a: Usually the hose has a dip, kink or uphill section, or it's too long and coiled. It can also be a clogged screen at the port or a missing internal fitting. Shorten and straighten the hose, clean the port and recheck the setup diagram in your manual.

faqs.q: Is there a small dehumidifier with a drain hose?
faqs.a: Yes. The Frigidaire FFAD2233W1 is a 22-pint single-room unit with the same 3/4-inch hose port as larger models, so a bedroom, bathroom or laundry closet with a nearby drain can run hands-free.
